moat_against: Advertising spend is highly cyclical — a recession cuts revenue directly
Competition for ad budgets from online/social platforms
Ground-lease renewals, zoning and permit regulation can erode or displace sites
High leverage: net debt $3.354B plus $1.487B lease liabilities (dcf_numbers.json)
moat_for: Scarce, permit-restricted billboard locations that are largely irreplaceable in high-traffic corridors
Largest US outdoor network and scale, concentrated in secondary/local markets with an entrenched local sales force
Digital billboard scale — small share of faces drives a disproportionate share of billboard revenue, with programmatic growth
Stable ~67% gross margin and ROIC in the 12-17% range through 2021-2025 (fundamentals.json)
moat_justification: Scarce permitted billboard locations and the largest US outdoor network give durable local pricing power, with ROIC 12.3%/12.5%/14.7%/12.5%/17.1% in 2021-2025 and gross margin stable at ~67% (fundamentals.json), but advertising is cyclical, online/social platforms compete for the same budgets, leases and permits renew, and leverage is high — moderate moat, not wide.
name: Lamar Advertising Company
one_liner: Solid billboard REIT, moat 6/10 — does not clear 15% on owner's-earnings DCF (7.7% weighted IRR, IV@15% $61.14 vs $150.10 price; clears 15% only below ~$61); sector AFFO model fits better, so confidence is low.
